sentences.text: Shri Shyamlal Patidar, learned counsel for the appel  Shri Manoj Kumar Soni, learned counsel for the respo  ORDER
The appellant has filed this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 25.4.2023 passed in MACC No.291/2021 challenging quantum of compensation.
2. Short facts of the case are that on 29.11.2019 at around 5.30 in the morning the appellant was going from his home to his field for irrigating his crops.
He was walking by the roadside.

When he reached near Digthan- Pipaliya public road, respondent no.1 came riding motorcycle No.MP-09- VS-5920 in rash and negligent manner and dashed into the appellant, because of which he sustained fracture in the right lower limb near his ankle and foot.

He was treated at Aurobindo Hospital,
Indore, where he was underwent a x- ray examination in which it was found that below the tibia bone in medial malleolus bone fracture.

2.1 The appellant filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:29051 2 MA-4355-2023 Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him.

entities.text:
Motor NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:29051 2 MA-4355-2023 Vehicles Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The claims Tribunal after considering the evidence available on record awarded compensation of Rs.1,14,000/- to the appellant.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant has suffered permanent disability, which was duly proved by the evidence of Dr. Devendra Mandloi (AW-2), who has issued certificate of permanent disability Ex.P/22, whereby it was certified that appellant has suffered 84% permanent disability into his right leg.
As such, he is entitled for compensation for sustaining permanent disability.

However, the claims Tribunal has not believed the same and has not awarded anything,
which is not correct in view of the clear statement of Dr. Devendra Mandloi (AW-2) as well as the certificate of permanent disability.
Thus, he prays for enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text:
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.3/Insurance Company points out that Dr.
Devendra Mandloi was not the treating doctor.

The appellant was treated at Aurobindo Hospital,
Indore, then M.Y.Hospital, Indore and Sevalaya Hospital, Indore, but he has not produced any certificate from any of these hospitals, which goes to show that he has managed the certificate and that too after more than two and half years of filing claim petition.
He also points out that he had certified that there is restriction in movement of hip joint.
However, the injury was near the ankle of the right leg of the appellant.
He, thus submits that the certificate is not believable.

He, therefore,
supports the findings of the award and prays for dismissal of the appeal.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29051 3 MA-4355-2023 5.
Heard learned counsel for the parties; perused the record.
6. On a close scrutiny of the permanent disability Ex.P/22 it had come to the fore that Dr. Devendra Mandloi observed that the appellant was not able to run properly.
However, this certification has done by him is not based on any scientific method.

He has not clarified that there is restriction in hip joint, whereas there is simple fracture in the right ankle of the appellant, in the considered view of this Court the claims Tribunal has elaborately recorded the findings in para 17, 18 and 19 of the impugned award with respect to the injuries sustained by the appellant, which in the light of the evidence available on record is not required to be interfered.

7. However, considering the fact that appellant suffered injury of fracture and treated at three different hospitals and remained under treatment for long time a further lumpsum amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded to the appellant over and above the amount already awarded by the claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing claim application till its payment.
8. With the aforesaid, the appeal stands disposed off.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE patil Kansingh vs Shriram on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14916916/
